title: Two Processes That Need Each Other

scenes.tts: A sensor sits in a small creek in Virginia. It checks the oxygen in the water every fifteen minutes. On one summer day, the water held far more oxygen at six in the evening. It held less in the early morning. Why does creek oxygen go up and down? And if plants make their own food, why do they use oxygen too?
scenes.caption: A sensor sits in a small creek in Virginia. It checks the oxygen in the water every 15 minutes. On one summer day, the water held far more oxygen at 6 p.m. It held less in the early morning. Why does creek oxygen go up and down? And if plants make their own food, why do they use oxygen too?

scenes.tts: Look inside one green leaf cell. It has a chloroplast, a green part of the cell that takes in light. Here, photosynthesis happens. Photosynthesis uses radiant energy, such as light from the sun. It makes sugar, called glucose, and oxygen. Carbon dioxide and water go in. Sugar and oxygen come out.

scenes.narration: Look inside one green leaf cell. It has a chloroplast, a green part of the cell that takes in light. Here, photosynthesis happens. Photosynthesis uses radiant energy, such as light from the sun. It makes sugar, called glucose, and oxygen. Carbon dioxide and water go in. Sugar and oxygen come out.

scenes.tts: The same cell also has mitochondria. Mitochondria are found in almost all plant and animal cells. Most cellular respiration happens in them. Respiration joins sugar with oxygen. This releases energy the cell can use. Carbon dioxide and water come out, and some energy leaves as heat.

scenes.tts: A reactant is a substance that goes into a process. A product is a substance that comes out. The products of photosynthesis are the reactants of respiration. The products of respiration are the reactants of photosynthesis. Processes that depend on each other like this are interdependent. The same matter is used again.

scenes.tts: Energy moves differently. It flows one way. Light from the sun becomes chemical energy in sugar. Respiration releases that energy for the cell. Some of it leaves as heat. Energy changes form as it goes.
scenes.visual: one-way energy path: light, chemical energy in sugar, energy the cell can use, heat

scenes.tts: Think of the creek as a tub. The tap is running, and the drain is open. Sunlight turns the tap on. The tap is photosynthesis, adding oxygen. The drain never closes. The drain is respiration, by nearly every living thing. By day, the tap often runs faster, so oxygen climbs. After dark, only the drain is open, so oxygen tends to fall. Plants make new sugar only in light, but they respire day and night.
